Subject: Questions on Data Handling & Deletion Workflow — FinTechCo / Redwood

Hi Camila (and team),

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful. A few follow-up questions from our privacy and compliance teams around how Redwood handles customer data (specifically PII), retention, and deletion/RTBF workflows. High-level list below — can you confirm which items are supported and typical timelines?

1) What data does Redwood store by default for hosted inference (inputs/outputs, logs, usage metadata)?
2) For deletion requests (RTBF), what is the standard process and SLA from request to purge (primary store) and to purge from backups/snapshots?
3) Are logs (access logs, audit logs) retained separately? What defaults and can retention be shortened?
4) Data residency: we need EU-only storage and processing for EU customers — can Redwood guarantee that?
5) Do you offer deletion/audit proofs or a certificate of deletion?
6) Any constraints from cloud snapshots, disaster recovery, or long-term backups we should be aware of?

If easier, we can set up a short call with our security/compliance folks (Sam copied). We’re preparing a list of contractual additions that might include a 30-day primary purge and 90-day backup purge requirement — want to understand operational impact.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Privacy & Compliance
FinTechCo
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list and for the convo today. Quick post-call recap and initial answers. I’ll loop in our Security/Infra folks for exact timelines and to validate backups/snapshots constraints, but here’s where we stand operationally and next steps.

Summary answers (high level):
- Data retained by default: For hosted API, we do not use customer prompts to train models. We retain request/response logs and usage metadata for diagnostics and abuse prevention. Retention is configurable per account and defaults to 30 days.
- Deletion / RTBF: Customers submit a deletion request via support portal or API. We soft-delete records immediately (remove from primary index/accessible stores). Full purge from primary store is typically completed within 30 days for hosted plans. Backups & snapshots are handled by our infra provider and have longer retention — see notes below.
- Backups/snapshots: Cloud snapshot retention varies; typical timeline to remove data from historical snapshots is 90–180 days depending on snapshot rotation and regional providers. We’ll confirm exact guarantees for EU regions.
- Logs & audit: Access and audit logs are stored separately and retention can be configured; default is 90 days for audit logs but can be reduced for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Data residency: We can provision EU-only storage/processing for FinTechCo on Dedicated or Private. Hosted API supports region routing for EU but for strict residency Dedicated is recommended.
- Deletion proof: We can produce audit evidence of deletion actions (ticket + internal purge logs) and provide a signed attestation for enterprise contracts; for formal certification we can share SOC2 report and work with you on deletion attestations.

Open items / risks to confirm (I will escalate to Security/Infra):
- Exact backup/snapshot purge timeline for eu-west-1 (customer requirement of 90 days would be typical but we need confirmation).
- Whether we can guarantee zero retained decrypted copies in any cross-region replication paths for hosted plans.
- Any production DR/SLA constraints that require longer retention windows.

Next steps / asks:
- I’ll loop in Neha (security) / Marissa (CS) and propose a short 30–40 minute call to walk through the deletion flow and to align on contractual language.
- Olivia/Sam: can you share the specific RTBF clause/target SLA your legal team wants to include so we can map operationally?

Attachments: none in this message.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila/Vanessa — a few clarifications from our side following internal review:

- Deletion SLA expectations: FinTechCo policy requires customer data removed from primary stores within 30 calendar days of RTBF request.
- Backup purge: we require backups/snapshots containing customer-identifiable data to be purged within 90 days of the RTBF effective date. This includes cloud snapshots and any long-term backups.
- Logs: we are comfortable with 180-day retention for audit logs (to support investigations), but we require that logs containing PII be redacted or encrypted under customer-managed keys where possible.
- Residency: EU-only processing and storage is required for EU customers; cross-border replication is not allowed without explicit consent.
- Audit evidence: we will need a deletion certificate (signed attestation) for each purge event and a small sample of purge-audit records for SOC/audit review.

We understand there are infrastructure constraints (snapshots, provider retention windows). If Dedicated or Private gives us the controls we need (KMS, snapshot lifecycle control), we’re open to that as a contractual requirement.

I’ve attached a short doc summarizing our RTBF requirements. Can Neha or your infra/security team confirm whether the 90-day backup purge SLA is achievable on hosted/managed plans or only on Dedicated/Private?

[Attachment: FinTechCo-Rtbf-Reqs.pdf]

Thanks,
Sam Patel
